hypothesis: The bead lattice can be made stage-bright by porting lattice-interactive/3.frag's brightness structure, without flattening it and without touching the global multiplier
why: H10 as stated is REFUTED, but its GOAL is achieved by INVERTING the reference. lattice-interactive/3's structure is HIGH palette base (0.50) + LOW slope (0.36) + gamma 0.80 -- every one of those is a FLOOR-LIFTER. Ported literally it does make litPct explode (9.17 -> 80.5 at gamma 0.80) but darkPct collapses 14.8 -> 0.04: a grey wash, exactly the failure mode the brief forbade. The lattice-bead needs the OPPOSITE: palette base DOWN 0.33 -> 0.10 and lightness slope UP 0.40 -> 1.20, with gamma left ALONE (1.18 -> 1.24, i.e. slightly higher, not lower). Base lifts every pixel; slope lifts only lit pixels -- that is contrast instead of wash. Result triples the strong marks AND more than doubles the real black, on all three mon.

measured.cutoffs: litPct = Rec.709 luma > 20 (matches lab/kiku); brightPct = luma > 50; darkPct = luma < 8. Same cutoffs on every arm. bright>50 is the number that predicts whether it reads on a dark field.
measured.method: controller REMOVED, all four seeds pinned (seed 0.618/0.755/0.892/0.029) + paperCranes.seeds pinned, time pinned, FULL RESOLUTION 900x900 read off the LIVE canvas (no PNG round-trip, no downsampling). n=3 (t=4,8,16) x 3 mon. Port asserted by FILE CONTENT not by the port in the URL.
measured.parity: bright.frag with levers set to 1.frag's values reproduces 1.frag EXACTLY (lit 9.17=9.17, dark 14.80=14.80), so every delta is the lever alone

lever_contributions_hakkaku_litPct_from_.palette L BASE 0.33->0.10 (INVERTED): litPct +2.85, brightPct +5.74 (3.37->9.11), darkPct +22.3 -- the winning direction
lever_contributions_hakkaku_litPct_from_.palette L SLOPE 0.40->1.20 (NEW lever, n: the actual instrument: brightPct 3.37->9.57 at base 0.12
lever_contributions_hakkaku_litPct_from_.bg floor knob_159 0.5->0.8, PROPERLY ISO: +0.81 pt only, and halves the real black (14.8->6.9)
lever_contributions_hakkaku_litPct_from_.bg field BASE 0.30->0.00: -0.03 pt DEAD LEVER (alpha ~1 across the frame, the bg is never visible)

measured.EXB_ON_TRAP: line 188 EXB_ON = step(0.001, knob_151..knob_160). Setting ANY of knob_156/157/159/160 wakes ALL of them at their unset value of 0, which drives CHROMA to ~0 (greyscale) and GAIN to 0.66. The naive bg-floor test measures litPct 0.00 / darkPct 96.52 -- a near-black monochrome frame. This fully explains the earlier 'raising the bg floor goes flat and monochrome' observation: it was the gate, NOT the bg floor. Isolate by pinning knob_156/157/160 to the EXB-neutral 0.5.
measured.STAGE_vs_BASE: brightPct x2.70 (hakkaku) / x3.07 (kikko) / x3.08 (ume); darkPct x2.51 / x2.28 / x2.37. BOTH axes improve on every mon -- brighter AND blacker.
measured.small_scale_15pct: DECISIVE PASS. Downscaled to 135px (15%, the across-a-dark-room scale): BASE brightPct 0.15% and luma sd 6.6 -- it effectively DISAPPEARS, no strong marks survive. STAGE brightPct 8.32% (55x) and sd 18.3 (2.8x the structural contrast). This is the single most important number for a wall.
measured.hex_vs_bead: CONFIRMS the retraction of the -37.8% coverage loss: under my controlled instrument the bead GAINS coverage over hex (hex lit 7.98 / bright 1.83 / dark 36.4 vs bead lit 9.17 / bright 3.37 / dark 14.8). The bead is not darker than hex; it is LESS BLACK than hex, which is the real problem -- the bead trades hex's black field for a grey haze.
measured.aliasing_probe: In-shader 5-tap box filter sized to fwidth(uv), knob_176, as an independent probe of the mipmap hypothesis. At stage framing (navZoom 0.218) it recovers NOTHING (lit 9.17->9.18, bright 9.11->9.17). At extreme zoom-out (navZoom 0.06) it recovers ~3% (lit 12.49->12.88). Agrees with the coordinator's own mipmap measurement (17.75% of pixels change by mean 1.2/255, meanLum 18.64->18.58). VERDICT: residual darkness is LIGHTING, not coverage. Caveat: 5 taps cannot approximate a 97k-texel footprint, so this is a LOWER bound on the aliasing effect. image_filter=mipmap deliberately NOT in the projector URL.

hex_rebaseline_n3_kikko_spread_le_0.05pt.verdict: STAGE is a WHOLE-LATTICE-FAMILY fix, not a bead fix. On hex it is STRONGER: brightPct x4.71 (1.83->8.62) while darkPct RISES 36.4->56.6. On bead x3.06 with darkPct 15.7->36.0 -- i.e. STAGE restores HEX's native blackness (36.4%) to the bead while tripling its strong marks. Tuned and reported against the hex baseline as instructed.

measured.wrap_artifact_corroboration: Independently corroborates lab/whole's wrap-spill finding from the other side: I measured the bead as LESS BLACK than hex (dark 14.8% vs 36.4%) with alpha~1 across the whole frame, which is why the bg-field base tested as a DEAD lever (-0.03 pt driving it 0.30->0.00) -- the grey haze is not the background, it is REPEAT-wrap spill being drawn as lattice. Same phenomenon, two instruments. I have NOT relied on the +30-43% brightening figure; my premise is the lattice's own inherent darkness, and my headline numbers are now re-baselined against hex.

preset.note: The tuning is BAKED into bright.frag, so the URL carries NO lever knobs. knob_170 gamma / knob_173 palette base / knob_174 palette slope remain as optional live trims (omit = baked value). Drop the four seed params for per-device variety.

next: Bake the STAGE tuning (palette base 0.10, slope 1.20, gamma 1.24) into lattice-bead/1.frag itself -- it is a pure shading change, legal to make audio-reactive later, and it does not touch the global multiplier. Then re-run the other lab arms on the bright substrate, because every motif comparison so far was made at a tuning where the lattice is 3x too dim and the motif differences may not survive.
spawned: The palette lightness SLOPE is a lever nobody in the fan-out had listed, and it is the strongest contrast-preserving brightness control in the shader. Worth auditing every other lattice shader for the same base-vs-slope imbalance.

EXB_ON gates ten knobs together; any teammate who moves ONE of knob_151..160 silently moves the others to 0. This has almost certainly corrupted other measurements -- it should be documented in HANDOFF s14 as a measurement trap.
The bead cell's real deficit vs hex is LOST BLACK, not lost light (dark 14.8% vs hex 36.4%). Framing the bead problem as 'too dim' sent this run down the wrong lever for its first hour.
kikko and hakkaku both read at least as well as ume and gain MORE from the fix (3.07x / 2.70x vs ume 3.08x); kikko has the boldest large-scale structure and is my ship pick.

hypothesis: One large, un-folded, whole motif -- the bead itself -- presented as the subject, with the lattice as its field, produces recognition where the folded lattice cannot
evidence: journals/lab/shots/sheet-final-11-15pct.png (all 11 mon at the 15% dark-field proxy), journals/lab/shots/sheet-forced-choice.png + forced-choice-KEY.txt (3/4 correct at 25% chance), journals/lab/shots/sheet-alive.png (10 s long exposure + temporal motion map), journals/lab/shots/sheet-src.png (source silhouettes), journals/lab/shots/h-live-ume.png (controller ON)
why: CONFIRMED, and the wave-1 blocker did not have to be removed. fractal() was NOT rewritten. Wave 1 is right that the mirror-repeat fold lands its cell at a CORNER of the folded domain, so any function of p is 4-fold mirrored and the motif can never be nameable INSIDE the lattice. H11 sidesteps it: the motif is drawn once, whole, un-folded, in SCREEN space at hero scale, and the fold is demoted from 'the thing that must show the motif' to 'the material the motif is made of'. Every wave-1 win survives untouched. Recognition comes from FIVE parts, and removing any one of them measurably costs it: (1) an un-folded whole-motif SDF in screen space; (2) a crisp palette-lit OUTLINE on |hd|=0 -- the only feature that survives a 15% downscale intact; (3) SUBJECT/GROUND separation, the field outside dimmed to 0.38 and desaturated to 0.40 -- WITHOUT THIS THE MOTIF IS NOT NAMEABLE AT 15% SCALE, the bright busy lattice simply out-shouts it, and this was the single largest step in the whole run; (4) the APERTURE, the same field magnified+rotated+shifted inside the silhouette, so the bead is a lens rather than a decal and inherits the perpetual zoom ratchet; (5) BEVEL/RIM/contact-shadow off the SDF gradient so it reads as an object with depth. ALIVE, NOT A LOGO, and measured rather than asserted: one page load, controller OFF, samples 2.5 s apart, resampled to a common size (the dynamic-resolution scaler moves the canvas), the whole frame changes 60-72% of pixels and the BEAD INTERIOR changes 83-90% -- the interior is the liveliest region in the frame while the silhouette does not move at all. A 10 s long exposure still shows a crisp mon; the temporal-SD map is bright inside the silhouette and dark outside. COST, stated honestly: n=3, controller off, seeds pinned, frameCount 61 -- hero ON meanLum 49.60+-0.50 / lit>20 54.96%+-0.69 / bright>50 26.01%+-0.20 vs hero OFF 66.62+-0.57 / 63.22%+-1.16 / 50.67%+-1.01, i.e. -25.5% meanLum, -8.27pt lit>20, -24.66pt bright>50. That is the price of subject/ground separation and it is real, not noise. A counter-ratchet was applied in the same edit per HANDOFF 7.4: the first pass (QUIET 0.25, interior lum -0.30) cost -43.6% meanLum, and lifting the interior back (INL 0, QUIET 0.38) recovered +10.8 meanLum with no loss of 15%-scale recognition. FORCED CHOICE: 4 trials, each a 15%-downscaled render against 4 deliberately confusable source silhouettes in a seeded-shuffled order with the key written to a file before judging -- 3/4 correct against 25% chance. The single miss was ume picked when the answer was kikyo, and inspecting the SOURCE silhouettes shows ume and kikyo are near-identical 5-lobed blossoms: that is a collision in the MOTIF SET, not a failure of the render. TWO TRAPS PAID, recorded in hero.md: (a) never mix the interior toward a flat colour -- it fills the cell GAPS as well as the lines and the bead goes to a dead grey wash that is no longer made of lattice; rebuild the interior the way the exterior is built, weighted by alpha; (b) never scale uv about the screen centre for the lens -- screen centre is the fold's SYMMETRY CENTRE where every level's ring converges and lumAcc clips chalky white; HERO_SHIFT moves the interior sample into ordinary lattice. Also confirmed: ?time= does NOT pin iTime (Visualizer.js sets iTime from performance.now and ?time= only creates a separate `time` uniform), so a 'time ladder' is not a controlled comparison -- single-page-load sampling is.
spawned: ume and kikyo are near-identical 5-lobed silhouettes and are the only confusable pair in the set at 15% scale. Ship at most one of them, or differentiate them by INTERIOR treatment (hue / lens scale) rather than by outline.

The hero costs -24.7pt of bright>50. A brightness pass on the hero preset specifically (not the substrate) is worth one teammate: the light should come back INSIDE the bead, since that is where the eye already is.

?time= does not pin iTime. Every /lab measurement that used a 'time ladder' for determinism was uncontrolled. Worth a one-line fix in Visualizer.js (iTime: manualFeatures.time ?? time) which would make the whole lab's determinism story real.

The hero is screen-anchored, so panning moves the field and not the bead. A world-anchored variant -- the bead sits at a place you can walk up to, with the lattice as terrain -- is a different and possibly better product for a room-scale wall.

Multi-bead: the bracelet. iChannel1/3 are the previous frame and iChannel2 duplicates initialFrame, so only ONE image texture exists today; a small Visualizer.js change would let a set of beads share the wall. Serialisation point, one owner.

The dynamic-resolution scaler silently halved the canvas mid-run (900 -> 450) during motion capture. Any /lab script comparing frames must record canvas.width and resample, or it will report a resolution change as a shader effect.
